sites.name: Apollo 11 - Tranquility Base
sites.description_tech: Mare Tranquillitatis. Near the mean sub-Earth point: Earth stays high (~60-75 deg elevation depending on libration) and continuously visible; ~14.77 d synodic day/night cycle.
sites.description_edu: The first crewed Moon landing. From here, Earth hangs almost motionless high in the sky.
sites.source: NASA NSSDCA / LROC (Apollo 11 LM, 0.67409 N 23.47298 E)

sites.name: Apollo 17 - Taurus-Littrow
sites.description_tech: Taurus-Littrow Valley flanked by North and South Massif. Mid-latitude control case: Sun reaches ~70 deg elevation with continuous DTE.
sites.description_edu: The final Apollo mission. A mountain-ringed valley where the Sun climbs much higher than at the poles.
sites.source: NASA NSSDCA / LROC (Apollo 17 LM, 20.1908 N 30.7717 E)

sites.name: Shackleton Rim (Peak near Shackleton)
sites.mission: Artemis III Candidate Region / CSA Utility Rover ops
sites.description_tech: Shackleton crater rim (D ~21 km, depth ~4.2 km, PSR interior). Rim ridges illuminated > 80% of the year; grazing Sun (|e| < ~2 deg); DTE modulated every 27.21 d by latitudinal libration.
sites.description_edu: The rim of a crater near the south pole. Here the Sun almost never sets, skimming the horizon like an eternal sunset.
sites.source: Bussey et al. (2010), Icarus / NASA Artemis III Candidate Regions

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.mission: Artemis III Candidate Region / Relay & DTE Prime Site
sites.description_tech: Massif ~4.6-5.0 km tall facing the Earthward nearside (lon ~2.7 E): offers nearly uninterrupted DTE visibility and broad illumination windows on its ridge.
sites.description_edu: An enormous mountain near the south pole facing Earth: ideal for talking directly with home without relay satellites.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate landing regions / Basilevsky et al. (2019)

sites.name: Cabeus Crater (LCROSS impact site)
sites.description_tech: Depressed interior (-3.85 km) ringed by +1 to +2 km walls: permanently shadowed region (PSR) with water ice confirmed by LCROSS. Extreme case of solar and DTE topographic blockage.
sites.description_edu: A crater so deep its floor never sees the Sun. NASA discovered water ice here in 2009.
sites.source: Colaprete et al. (2010), Science - LCROSS impact 84.675 S, 48.725 W

sites.name: Mons Mouton (Leibnitz Beta Plateau) - IM-2 Athena
sites.description_tech: Elevated plateau (+5321 m above R=1737.4 km) on former Leibnitz Beta. Real CLPS south-polar landing site; nearly 360-deg unobstructed horizon with excellent DTE.
sites.description_edu: A high plateau near the south pole where the commercial lander Athena touched down in 2025.
sites.source: LROC (Athena location 84.7906 S, 29.1957 E; elevation +5321 m)

sites.name: Nobile Rim 1
sites.mission: Artemis III Candidate Region / Former VIPER Target
sites.description_tech: Elevated rim of Nobile crater (~85.4 S, 35.0 E). Combines access to nearby cold traps with well-illuminated ridges and favorable DTE visibility.
sites.description_edu: The rim of another large south polar crater studied by NASA and CSA for nearby ice exploration.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate landing regions

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 - Shiv Shakti Point
sites.description_tech: High southern latitude (-69.37 deg) outside the extreme polar zone: ~14-day day/night cycle with peak solar elevation ~21 deg and continuous DTE (Earth elevation ~18-25 deg).
sites.description_edu: The site where India landed its Pragyan rover in 2023 in the southern lunar highlands.

sites.name: Chang'e 4 - Statio Tianhe (Von Karman)
sites.description_tech: South Pole-Aitken basin on the lunar farside (lon 177.6 E): Earth elevation < -35 deg at all times (DTE = 0%, requires Queqiao relay satellite). Mandatory negative control case for DTE.
sites.description_edu: The first spacecraft on the Moon's far side. Earth is never visible from here, so it relies on a relay satellite to communicate.

hardware_profiles.name: CSA LEAP Micro-Rover / Surface Payload (0.5 m)
hardware_profiles.description_tech: Typical camera/panel height on microrovers and surface payloads in the CSA Lunar Exploration Acceleration Program (LEAP).
hardware_profiles.description_edu: A low-profile Canadian mini-rover (half a meter): any nearby rock or hill can block its sunlight.

hardware_profiles.name: CSA Canadian Utility Rover Mast (1.5 m)
hardware_profiles.description_tech: Navigation mast, DTE antenna, and solar panels on the Canadian Space Agency (CSA) Utility Rover, an official Resources partner.
hardware_profiles.description_edu: Canada's utility rover (1.5 meters tall), designed to assist astronauts at the lunar south pole.

hardware_profiles.name: Artemis Astronaut EVA / Standard Tripod (2.0 m)
hardware_profiles.description_tech: Standard reference height (2.0 m) for an EVA astronaut visor or deployable communications/solar tripod.
hardware_profiles.description_edu: The eye height of an astronaut or a portable tripod antenna placed on the surface (2 meters).

hardware_profiles.name: Artemis Lunar Terrain Vehicle / Rover High-Gain (2.2 m)
hardware_profiles.description_tech: High-gain X/Ka-band antenna and deployed solar array mounted on a pressurized rover or Lunar Terrain Vehicle (LTV).
hardware_profiles.description_edu: The astronauts' lunar rover with its communication antenna raised to 2.2 meters.

hardware_profiles.name: NASA CLPS Lander Top Deck / Solar Array (3.5 m)
hardware_profiles.description_tech: Upper deck of a commercial CLPS lander (e.g. Nova-C Athena / Griffin, ~3.5 m), maximizing visibility over local terrain undulations.
hardware_profiles.description_edu: The top deck of a commercial lunar lander (3.5 meters), ideal for seeing over nearby boulders and ridges.
